verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
cold light on the cobblestones—
someone's dropped glove
still waiting for a hand

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the pigeons peck close
mistaking bent fingers of cloth
for something worth keeping

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a child returns at dusk,
checks the same corner twice,
walks home with empty hands

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the glove goes stiff with frost—
by morning even hope
has forgotten its shape

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone else's boots
pause, then step around it—
the city keeps walking

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a woman picks it up now
shakes off the night's cold
and slips it on her hand

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the fit is close enough—
she walks off in someone else's warmth,
not looking back for the pair

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
streetlight flickers once
as if to remember something—
then lets the dark have it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bus pulls away
carrying half a conversation—
the rest waits at the curb

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
rain starts before she notices
her collar already turned up—
some habits arrive before the weather

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the coffee cup cools
on a windowsill no one owns anymore—
steam kept its own counsel

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a moth taps the glass
mistaking the porch light for morning—
someone finally turns it off

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the porch light dims
but the moth's shadow lingers
on the closed curtain

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning finds the curtain
still holding its small shadow—
the sun asks no questions

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone folds the curtain
into a drawer for later—
the shadow stays behind
